problem: Topological-map memories for visual navigation suffer from redundant nodes and wrong edge connections because of the gap between the spatial (odometry) and perceptual (appearance) domains. Existing memory structures also do not focus on the parts of memory relevant to the goal cue when generating a policy.
motivation: Reliable policies for autonomous robots depend on well-maintained spatial memory. A topological graph is compact, but only if it is built accurately online. Fusing pose and appearance cues should give a cleaner graph, and goal-conditioned attention over it should give better policies.
key_idea: Build the topological memory online by fusing odometry pose estimation with perceptual similarity, then extract goal-relevant graph features with a GNN-based topology multi-factor transformer (TMFT) that uses multi-factor attention.
insight: Not derivable from the abstract alone. The abstract claims that fusing spatial and perceptual cues fixes node redundancy and wrong edges, and that the multi-factor attention over the graph improves policy generation. No ablation details are available.
method: Online topology construction: builds the graph incrementally by fusing odometry pose estimation with perceptual similarity estimation to decide node creation and edge connection.
Fusion of spatial and perceptual domains: reduces node redundancy and incorrect edge connections caused by the distribution gap between the two domains.
Topology multi-factor transformer (TMFT): a differentiable graph extraction structure that uses graph neural networks to integrate global memory.
Multi-factor attention: emphasizes graph elements closely related to the goal cues for policy generation.
Learning-based visual navigation policy: image-goal navigation policy conditioned on the topological memory features.
